profile.profile:
Cousins Richard Bevan and Joshu Doherty. Based in East London & Glasgow, respectively.

Their debut release in 2000 was a series of handmade CDs simply called "Posthuman" (though better known by the colour of the card inserts - grey, black, blue and brown). The duo then went on to host a number of parties in an abandoned underground train station in London between 2001 and 2004, and founded their own label [l=Seed Records (2)] with which they released 3 albums and several other releases of their own and other artists' material. They also were the first act on Manchester based imprint [l=Skam]'s SMAK sublabel.

Doherty left Seed Records to help relaunch UK techno imprint [l=B12] Records in 2006, and started a new label [l=Balkan Vinyl] in 2010.

In 2007, Doherty founded acid-focused clubnight "I Love Acid" along with [a=Luke Vibert] who's track it was named after, where Posthuman are resident DJs. It won "Best Club Event" in DJ Magazine's Best of British awards 2019. In 2014 the clubnight launched a vinyl-only label also named [l=I Love Acid]. He also performed as one half of [a=Altern 8]'s live shows between 2015 and 2020. Since 2021 Doherty has worked for the [l=Mobineko Multimedia] pressing plant.

The Trio of Doom was a short-lived jazz fusion power trio consisting of John McLaughlin on guitar, Jaco Pastorius on bass, and Tony Williams on drums. They were brought together by Columbia Records in 1979 to play the Havana Jam festival in Cuba alongside Billy Joel, Kris Kristofferson, Rita Coolidge, and others.

profile.profile: Daft Punk were a French electronic music duo formed in 1993 by [a=Thomas Bangalter] (born January 3, 1975) and [a=Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo] (born February 8, 1974). Bangalter and de Homem-Christo were previously in the rock band [a=Darlin'] with [a=Laurent Brancowitz]. After Brancowitz left the group to join his brother's band, [a=Phoenix], the remaining duo formed Daft Punk. On February 22, 2021, it was announced that they had disbanded for unknown reasons.

Please credit "as on release" - see also [l=Tuff Gong Ltd.], [l=Tuff Gong Music Ltd]/[l=Tuff Gong Music], [l=Tuff Gong International], [l=Tuff Gong Productions Ltd.].
For the studio, please see [l=Tuff Gong Recording Studio].

Tuff Gong was originally based on Orange Street before moving to 56 Hope Road, which is now the home of the Bob Marley Museum and The Bob Marley Theatre. The company subsequently moved to 220 Marcus Garvey Drive, and includes a recording studio, mastering room, stamper room, pressing plant, cassette plant, wholesale record shop, booking agency, as well as offices for Rita Marley Music and Ghetto Youths International.

profile.profile:
Multinational label.
[b]Label Code: LC 0149 / LC 00149[/b]

[B][U]Unofficial[/U] releases which have a printed "CBS" logo can be found here: [L=CBS (2)][/B]

The CBS label may also appear on a few releases as CBS Records, which also goes here. 

[l567392], former owner of the various CBS companies, was established in 1928, and in 1961, its recorded music division CBS Records was founded although the CBS brand did not appear until 1962 (as below) with the exception of South Africa which (independently of this process) was using CBS from 1 January 1956. It was initially set up to distribute and market releases on the CBS label overseas, from their US catalog owned by their subsidiary [l269353].

This was mainly for [l1866] releases due to trademark copyrights. [l567392] couldn't use that brand outside the US, because [l293204] (EMI) subsidiary [l97841] (later [l253617]) owned the rights to the [l1866] brand in most of the rest of the world, and [l213761] still has the rights to the name in Japan.

[l567392] set up a number of companies to market CBS releases. In Europe, the first to launch was the UK, where the CBS label was launched on May 1, 1962. It was initially distributed by [l293581]  until the acquisition of [l142275] in 1964, which was renamed [l1105348] on April 1, 1965, and subsequently took this role. The rest of Europe followed. Greece was in September 1962, Spain in October, Italy, Denmark, Norway, Finland and Sweden were in December 1962, [l109547] in France, [l286313] in the Netherlands and [l46221] in Germany were all in February 1963. 

South and Central America introduced the CBS label in August 1962 and Asia in July of the same year.

In Australia and New Zealand, the CBS label replaced the [l=Coronet (2)] label in January 1963.

These companies also used the CBS label to release records by locally signed artists.

In 1981 CBS introduced CX noise reduction technology for vinyl records and started to release CX encoded records. To properly play those records user is required to use CX encoder.
Playback without decoder is possible but then quality is potentially worse then for non CX encoded records. CX encoded records (from CBS or other record labels) are noted with [url=https://i.discogs.com/KKJJUSK8GON_WL5WZtHDNKab981zSOGFhYwI1Bxx6fo/rs:fit/g:sm/q:90/h:78/w:151/czM6Ly9kaXNjb2dz/LWRhdGFiYXNlLWlt/YWdlcy9MLTMwNzIt/MTc2MTcyOTI0NC02/NDIwLnBuZw.jpeg]CX logo[/url] on the record label or cover. Additionally for CBS all records with catalog number starting with 'CBS CX' are CX encoded. But CBS was also releasing those records with normal release numbers.   

Please put "CX Encoded" text in Format Free Text field to properly tag CX encoded releases.

On January 5, 1988, CBS Records, including the sublabels [l1866] and [l1005], were sold by [l211334] (formerly known as [l567392]) to [l353657] of Japan. [l211334] granted [l353657] a temporary license to use the CBS brand for three years. [l353657] acquired the international rights for [l1866] from [l63404] on October 15, 1990.

[l353657] began using [l1866] as a worldwide label instead of CBS on January 1, 1991, except in Spain and Japan, where the rights were owned respectively by [l1003] and [l213761] The holding company [l64672] was renamed [l19795] on the same date. The rights to the CBS brand were returned to [l211334] [l353657] acquired the rights for [l1866] in Spain on August 5, 2004 when [l53569] was established.

On December 15, 2006, [l272286], the successor of [l211334], revived the CBS Records brand. The label uses CBS' television networks and its other mass media platforms to market their artists. They also release soundtracks of CBS television shows. The new CBS Records label is not related to the former CBS Records business or its artists or assets.
